claude_proposed_widenings.name: heterogeneous_random_table_branch_payload
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The existing activation-family random table can only branch into ActivationPhase sequences. Wand of Wonder needs table rows that branch into different mechanics families, including uncontrolled creature summoning and sustained environmental phenomena, so a generic table-branch payload or cross-family composition is required.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: "A magically formed creature appears in an unoccupied space as close to the chosen point of origin as possible. The creature isn't under your control, acts as it normally would, and disappears after 1 hour or when it drops to 0 Hit Points."

claude_proposed_widenings.name: create_obscurement_field
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: Several rows create temporary areas that are Lightly or Heavily Obscured. The current effect vocabulary has no honest way to represent obscuring weather or swarms without pretending they are targeting blocks or conditions.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: "Heavy rain falls for 1 minute ... During that time, the area of effect is Lightly Obscured." / "The butterflies remain for 10 minutes, during which time the area of effect is Heavily Obscured."

claude_proposed_widenings.name: target_selection.closest_to_point_with_fallback_or_random_subject
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: Multiple rows target the creature closest to the chosen point, randomly choose among multiple possible subjects, or fall back to the user if the nearest target is ineligible. The current attachment/selection grammar does not express nearest-to-point targeting, GM-random subject choice, or invalid-target fallback.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: "If an effect has multiple possible subjects, the GM determines randomly which among them are affected." / "The creature closest to the chosen point of origin is enlarged ... If the target isn't you and can't be affected by that spell, you become the target instead."
